details:
**1997 handover from Britain to China**
Britain transferred sovereignty over the territory to the People's Republic of China on July 1, 1997. Hong Kong Island had been ceded to Britain in the 1842 Treaty of Nanking after the First Opium War, and the New Territories were leased in 1898 for 99 years.

**Kowloon Walled City**
A former Chinese military fort on the Kowloon Peninsula that became an almost ungoverned enclave controlled by triads. It was the densest settlement ever built, so packed with staircases and passages that one could cross it without touching the ground. It was demolished in the early 1990s and replaced by a park, with only its old Yamen building preserved. Planes landing at nearby Kai Tak airport passed just above it.

**Special Administrative Region and "One country, two systems"**
The territory is governed as a Special Administrative Region of China, as is nearby Macau, under the "one country, two systems" principle, which promised it its own legal and economic system and a high degree of autonomy. Its head of government is the Chief Executive, a post held by Carrie Lam from 2017 to 2022.

**Pearl River Delta and Macau**
The city lies at the mouth of the Pearl River, east of the former Portuguese colony of Macau, which was handed back to China in 1999. Together with Guangzhou and Shenzhen (which borders it to the north) it forms a giant megalopolis, and the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge links it across the delta. Its Hong Kong dollar circulates widely in Macau.

**Victoria Harbour and the Star Ferry**
The deep natural harbor between Hong Kong Island and the Kowloon Peninsula. The Star Ferry has carried passengers across it for over a century and is a famous tourist attraction.

**Kowloon Peninsula and the New Territories**
The territory's mainland portion. Kowloon lies south of Boundary Street, and the New Territories stretch north from there to the border with Shenzhen. Kowloon includes the Avenue of Stars honoring film celebrities and the seedy Chungking Mansions.

**Octopus card and the MTR**
The Octopus card is a contactless smart card used to pay for rides on the Mass Transit Railway (MTR) and also accepted by many shops. The MTR even has a line serving Hong Kong Disneyland.

**Lantau Island**
The territory's largest island, home to Hong Kong Disneyland (built on reclaimed land), the Po Lin Monastery, and the giant bronze Tian Tan "Big Buddha," reached by the Ngong Ping 360 cable car. The Tsing Ma Bridge, part of the Lantau Link, connects it to the rest of the city.

**Victoria Peak and the Peak Tram**
Victoria Peak is the highest hill on Hong Kong Island, reached by the Peak Tram funicular from the Central business district. The territory's overall highest point is Tai Mo Shan in the New Territories.

**Skyscrapers: International Commerce Centre, Bank of China Tower, HSBC Building**
The city has more skyscrapers than any other in the world. The 118-story International Commerce Centre in West Kowloon is the tallest and has the Sky100 observation deck. I. M. Pei designed the angular Bank of China Tower, and Norman Foster designed the HSBC headquarters.

**Chek Lap Kok airport and Cathay Pacific**
The current international airport was built on an island flattened and expanded by land reclamation, replacing Kai Tak in 1998. It is the hub of Cathay Pacific and one of the busiest airports in Asia.

**2019 extradition bill protests**
Massive pro-democracy protests erupted in 2019 against the Fugitive Offenders amendment bill, which would have allowed extradition to mainland China. Protesters occupied the airport in August 2019, and the bill was eventually withdrawn.

**Umbrella Movement**
The 2014 student-led pro-democracy protests, named for the umbrellas protesters used against police pepper spray. Their center was the Admiralty district, the site of the former HMS Tamar British naval base.

**"Fragrant Harbor"**
The literal meaning of the city's name in Cantonese (Heung Gong; Xianggang in Mandarin), its main spoken language.

**Cheung Chau Bun Festival**
An annual spring festival on Cheung Chau island featuring three 60-foot towers covered in buns, which participants race to climb. The city's emblem is the bauhinia flower, the Hong Kong orchid tree.
